 Order

This sixth application for grant of bail in the form of criminal appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed assailing the order dated 17.02.2025 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, District Singrauli, Headquarer-Waidhan (M.P.), whereby application under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of regular bail filed on behalf of appellant/accused has been dismissed.
2. Appellant has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. bearing Crime No.1040/2022 dated 28.10.2022 registered at Police Station-Sarai, District- Singrauli (MP) for commission of offence under Sections 376, 450 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w)(i), 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Appellant/accused is in detention since 14.12.2022.

3. Appellant's earlier four bail applications in the form of criminal appeal NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17117 2 CRA-3072-2025 under Section 14-A of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act were dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide orders dated 09.01.2023, 27.06.2023,
18.12.2023, 05.08.2024 passed in CRA No.12512/2022, CRA No.6337/2023, CRA No.13214/2023,
CRA No.7736/2024 respectively.

His fifth bail application was dismissed being time barred vide Brijesh Kumar Jaiswal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17270909/
1 order dated 04.02.2025 passed in CRA No.793/2025.

entities.text: Brijesh Kumar Jaiswal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, vide order dated 09.01.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.12512/2022, liberty was granted to the applicant to revive the prayer for grant of bail after examination of material witnesses or production of FSL report.
4. As per the prosecution story, on 26.10.2022 at around 08:00 pm, applicant trespassed into the house of prosecutrix and committed rape.
It is alleged that when she raised noise, her brother-in-law reached there and caught hold the present applicant.
FIR was registered.
After investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
Appellant is facing trial.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant is in detention since 14.12.2022 i.e. almost a period of two years & four months.
He has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
It is submitted that prosecutrix and other witnesses have already been examined before the Trial Court.
It is a false case.
It is further submitted that FSL report has been received and on vaginal slide of the prosecutrix, no human sperm has been found; even on her cloths and pubic hairs, no sperm has been found.
On the aforesaid pretext, it is prayed that appellant may be released on bail.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the victim/objector have opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the appellant.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17117 3 CRA-3072-2025 7.
Appellant is in detention for almost a period of two years & four months.
Prosecutrix has already been examined before the Trial Court.

Therefore, having taken into consideration the detention period of the applicant and FSL report including other material placed on record, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the appellant is not warranted.

Consequently, this appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 stands allowed and impugned order dated 17.02.2025 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, District Singrauli, Headquarer-Waidhan (MP) is set-aside.
8.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, District Singrauli
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is directed that appellant - Brijesh Kumar Jaiswal be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023.
9.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE @shish Brijesh Kumar Jaiswal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17270909/
